newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gabon leader meets Mobutu, slams rebel Tutsis.
newsitem.headline: Gabon leader meets Mobutu, slams rebel Tutsis.

text.p: Gabonese head of state Omar Bongo met convalescing Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko on Sunday and afterward slammed Tutsi rebels who have been fighting Zairean and Hutu forces in eastern Zaire.
"You take care of them, you feed them, and then one fine day they want to take over," Bongo said of the Tutsi forces.
Bongo told reporters that the planned multinational force for the region should solve Zaire's problems by restoring peace to the area and helping the refugees return home in Rwanda.

"All of the parties will have to understand -- Zaire, Burundi and Rwanda -- that everyone must return home and that we must facilitate the return home of the refugees. That's all," he said after 45 minutes of talks at the palatial French Riviera villa where Mobutu has been recovering from prostate cancer surgery in Switzerland.
Under a U.N.-approved plan, a multinational peace force under Canadian leadership is to be dispatched to eastern Zaire to help refugees stranded by the fighting.

The mission has had an uncertain start after hundreds of thousands of the refugees it was intended to help began streaming back home to Rwanda, prompting Washington to consult allies over whether the plan should be modified.
Mobutu, who has been keeping a low profile since arriving at his villa from Switzerland on November 4, held talks on Saturday with Zairean Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo.
The premier told reporters afterwards that Mobutu, who has appeared weak and thin during his few recent public appearances, would soon return to Kinshasa.
